tester_additions.reason: Pre-existing test_speculative_sampling.py only exercised multi_round_speculative_sampling on hand-picked deterministic (token, u) scenarios -- it never checked the algorithm's actual theorem (paper Appendix A.2: 'Output: a sample x ~ p'), i.e. that the RETURNED TOKEN'S MARGINAL DISTRIBUTION over many trials equals p_target for k>=2 sibling candidates each drawn from its own p_hat_i. That is exactly the property draft_tree.verify_tree leans on to claim a tree draft (multiple sibling candidates, not a single chain candidate) still preserves the output distribution -- a genuinely new claim beyond ch28's single-candidate case (dossier explicitly scopes the single-candidate accept/reject proof to ch28 Sec.28.5, not re-derived here). Added a fixed-seed (20260706), N=40000-trial, atol=0.02 Monte Carlo test per the tester contract's primer-chapter rule ('distribution-preserving mechanisms get a statistical test'). All 4 new cases (k=1 sanity, k=2 with mismatched drafts, k=3, and target==one-of-the-drafts edge case) pass deterministically.
